# MLForge v0.3.0 - Project Report

**What it is:** a pure-NumPy machine-learning library and research-style repository whose distinguishing feature is **measurable evidence of correctness**.
v0.3.0 turns the v0.2 engineering project into something that can be *checked from outside*: tests that are themselves tested, a real-data result anyone can reproduce,
and release materials prepared for the steps that need your accounts.

## 1. Measured status (all figures from `docs/correctness.md`, regenerated by `tools/build_dashboard.py`)

| | v0.2.0 | v0.3.0 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Estimators | 38 | **40** (+ conv / pooling / LSTM layers) |
| Tests | 291 | **402**, 0 failing |
| Line coverage | 98.5% | **98.6%** |
| Property-based (Hypothesis) laws | 0 | 21 |
| Mutation score (sampled) | not measured | **207 / 220 = 94.1%** |
| Gradient checks re-computed each run | - | 13, worst relative error 8.8e-10 |
| Benchmarked algorithms vs scikit-learn | 27 | 29 |
| Real-data result | - | **MNIST: CNN 98.57%, MLP 97.82%** |

## 2. What was done for each requested item

**1. Put it in public with checkable claims** - *prepared; the account-bound steps are yours.*
Done: MkDocs site (builds in strict mode), GitHub Pages / docs / dashboard / weekly-mutation workflows (valid YAML), `docs/RELEASING.md` (step-by-step), `.zenodo.json`, `scripts/set_repo_url.py`,
and a PyPI check that found **`mlforge` is already taken** (by an unrelated project that also installs a top-level `mlforge` module). The distribution is now `mlforge-numpy`, and
`scripts/rename_package.py` renames the import package - verified by renaming a full copy of the project and passing the entire suite under the new name (which also exposed and fixed a bug in the script itself).
*Not possible here:* pushing to GitHub, running CI, publishing to PyPI, minting a Zenodo DOI.

**2. Real-scale results** - *mostly done.* `Conv2D` (im2col, stride, padding), `MaxPool2D`, `Flatten`, `LSTM` (BPTT) with finite-difference gradient checks and comparisons against naive reference loops.
Real MNIST (checksum-verified): a 5,258-parameter CNN reaches **98.57%** in ~97 s on one CPU core; results are deterministic and saved weights re-evaluate identically.
*Not done:* CIFAR-10 (not reachable from this sandbox, and a NumPy CNN large enough for it would take hours), and a transformer (weeks of work; not attempted).

**3. Verification beyond coverage** - *done.* 21 Hypothesis properties (found 2 real bugs); a mutation-testing tool (baseline-must-pass guard) over 22 modules, 207/220 killed, 30+ genuine test gaps closed, the 13 survivors individually reviewed as equivalent; a generated correctness dashboard with SVG badges and a CI job.

**4. Close the cheap speed gaps** - *partly, with analysis for the rest.* Histogram gradient boosting: **2.3x / 6.3x / 12.6x faster** than exact boosting at 2k / 8k / 32k rows (quality equal or better; but 1.5-4.5x *slower* than scikit-learn on the small benchmark data).
The perceptron was analysed and **left alone**: its updates are inherently sequential, so a vectorised form cannot beat the current loop on non-separable data. A KD-tree was **not built**: per-query Python overhead exceeds one BLAS matrix multiply at every size benchmarked.

**5. Write-up and credential** - *written; submission is yours.* `paper.md` + `paper.bib` in JOSS format (author block left as TODO - I cannot invent identities) and an essay, *How do you know your ML implementation is correct?*
JOSS typically expects a public history and users; see `RELEASING.md`. Acceptance cannot be guaranteed or influenced from here.

## 3. Bugs found by the new evidence layers

| Found by | Bug |
|---|---|
| Hypothesis | `StandardScaler` returned +-1 for constant columns with an inexact floating-point mean |
| Hypothesis | **Infinite recursion** in tree growth for feature values one ulp apart |
| Mutation testing | `recall_score` could return F1 and no test would fail (test data had precision == recall) |
| Mutation testing | RMSProp's update formula, optimizer defaults, ReLU's negative-input gradient, silhouette singletons, ... untested |
| Renamed-copy test | the rename script left `mlforge_*` data keys half-renamed |
| Reading outputs | a notebook claimed gradient descent matched the closed form while not converged; several README figures were mis-stated and corrected |
